previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of type II diabetes, morbid obesity, atrial fibrillation, and chronic foot ulcers was admitted with chills and found to have gas gangrene of the right first toe. He underwent amputation and a subsequent debridement with wound vac placement. His postoperative course was complicated by sepsis, hypotension, and acute kidney injury, requiring ICU monitoring. He was treated with IV antibiotics, later transitioned to ertapenem via PICC line for six weeks. His heart failure was managed with diuresis, and his warfarin was adjusted after an elevated INR. He was stabilized and discharged to an extended care facility for ongoing IV antibiotic therapy and wound care.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Diabetes with peripheral circulatory disorders, type II or unspecified type, uncontrolled
Ulcer of other part of foot
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health

# Right foot erythema/discharge: Patient presented with mild 
increase in erythema surrounding prior open amputation site with 
increased yellow granulation tissue overlying wound. No evidence 
of infection at this time without leukocytosis or left shift, 
fevers, chills, spreading erythema or concerning radiologic 
changes. Some of this may be due to increased weight bearing on 
foot leading to erythema and increased blood flow with 
subsequent increased discharge/granulation tissue. He was 
evaluated by podiatry in the ED the night of presentation and 
the following morning they saw him again and did bedside 
debridement. They were not concerned for infection. Plan to 
continue PO suppressive augmentin and hold off on further IV 
antibiotics was discussed with outpatient providers. Patient 
knows to seek care again if wound changes in appearance or if 
fevers, chills, increased pain, etc. He will call his podiatrist 
first thing ___ morning (phone # included in discharge 
paperwork) to schedule graft and closure now that he has filed 
with ___.
